rules: When the child-safe story arc, exact page text, character direction, and approval state are locked for illustration.
When all requested picture-book pages are produced, visually inspected, and ready for continuity and safety review.
When a page needs visual, continuity, readability, safety, or exact-text correction before production.
When every page passes review and the approved page set is ready for ordered digital or print assembly.
When exports and mechanical QA are complete and the coordinator needs the final package status and any residual risks.
When packaging finds a story or wording issue that the author must decide.
When the approved brief or storyboard is missing, contradictory, or needs a story, wording, age, reading-level, or page-count decision before illustration can continue.
When review finds a story, source wording, age-fit, reading-level, or storyboard defect that the author must decide before the page can be fixed.
When the review report's approval or approved page manifest is missing, incomplete, or contradicts the requested pages.
When an approved page has a visual or text-surface defect that packaging must not repair.
